ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Six integers are marked on the real line (see the fig.). It is known that at least two of them are divisible by 3, and at least two of them are divisible by 5. Which numbers are divisible by 15?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a number line, and six points A, B, C, D, E, F are marked on equally spaced tick marks; counting to the right from A, B is at 3 spaces, C is at 5 spaces, D is at 10 spaces, E is at 12 spaces, and F is at 15 spaces. Let the integer on A be n, then the six integers are respectively n, n+3, n+5, n+10, n+12, n+15. Then reason: Look modulo 3. The remainders of the offsets 0, 3, 5, 10, 12, 15 are respectively 0, 0, 2, 1, 0, 0. If n is not 0 mod 3, then it is impossible for there to be at least two points satisfying divisibility by 3; for at least two to both be divisible by 3, it can only be n ≡ 0 (mod 3). Look modulo 5. The remainders of the offsets 0, 3, 5, 10, 12, 15 are respectively 0, 3, 0, 0, 2, 0. If n is not 0 mod 5, then it is also impossible for there to be at least two points satisfying divisibility by 5; for at least two to both be divisible by 5, it can only be n ≡ 0 (mod 5). Therefore n is divisible by both 3 and 5, that is, n is divisible by 15, so A is divisible by 15. Also F = n + 15, and is also divisible by 15. The other points are not necessarily divisible by 15.

method.method_draft: First describe/read the figure: the six labeled points lie on equally spaced integer ticks of a number line. Counting tick intervals from A gives positions A=0, B=3, C=5, D=10, E=12, F=15 relative to A. Let the integer at A be n, so the labeled integers are n, n+3, n+5, n+10, n+12, n+15. Use the text condition that at least two are divisible by 3 and at least two are divisible by 5. Modulo 3, the offsets have residues: A,B,E,F are 0; C is 2; D is 1. Since only the offset-residue-0 group contains at least two labels, n must be 0 mod 3. Modulo 5, the offsets have residues: A,C,D,F are 0; B is 3; E is 2. Since only that group contains at least two labels, n must be 0 mod 5. Thus A is divisible by both 3 and 5, and F=A+15 is also divisible by both. The other labeled points are not in both forced groups, so the numbers divisible by 15 are A and F.
